item.description: Since 2025, the traditional gray uniform of the Swiss army is assigned only for representative tasks, generating savings of about 55 million.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Since 2025, Tenuta A has been assigned only for representational duties. - Recoverable uniforms are inspected, repaired and redistributed. - Those that can no longer be used end up in incineration plants. - The projected savings are around 55 million francs.
## Key facts - Where → Bern - Uniform → Tenuta A, traditional gray uniform - Since 2025 → assigned only to military personnel with representational duties - Savings → around 55 million francs - 1993 purchase → 180,000 uniforms for 114 million francs - Assessment by the Swiss Federal Audit Office → up to 100 million francs in savings
On September 26, 2026, from Bern, the Swiss Army confirmed that the traditional gray uniform is being phased out and that discarded garments, when they can no longer be salvaged, are taken to a waste incineration plant. The news was reported by Schweiz Heute, the national news portal of CH Media.
Since 2025, the so-called Tenuta A has no longer been issued on a large scale. Distribution has continued for military personnel engaged in representational duties, including members of the military band. The Army links ending general distribution to overall savings of around 55 million francs.
The handling of the garments follows a precise distinction. Uniforms that are still usable are inspected, repaired and, if necessary, redistributed. Those that can no longer be salvaged instead go to the incinerator. The phase-out thus leads to the accumulation of thousands of uniforms, but the Army does not record the total number of gray uniforms intended for disposal.
### Why there is no second-hand market
Sale is ruled out because the uniform is still in use and the Army wants to avoid the risk of improper use. Recycling is also not considered a sensible alternative: first, both the uniforms and the insignia would have to be made unrecognizable, with the associated costs and work deemed excessive.
Tenuta A had already sparked discussion. Many soldiers considered the jacket and trousers uncomfortable and outdated. In 2021, Centre Council of States member Marianne Binder-Keller had called for a more modern uniform, but the request does not appear likely to materialize.
The financial precedent dates back to 1993. That year, Parliament approved the purchase of 180,000 uniforms for 114 million francs. Subsequently, the Swiss Federal Audit Office criticized the planning and argued that a better procurement procedure would have made it possible to save up to 100 million francs. These precedents accompany the current management and show that the debate over military supplies also has roots in Parliament's decisions and subsequent audits. ## The meaning of the figures
The most concrete fact for understanding the decision is the shift from large-scale distribution to targeted allocation. The source dates this choice from 2025 and links it to total savings of 55 million. To understand the scope of the decision, it is useful to keep three levels separate: the date of the distribution, the price of the historical purchase, and the handling of withdrawn garments.
### Three levels to keep separate
The 55 million francs are the total savings the army intends to achieve by abandoning large-scale distribution. The text does not present them as an annual figure or link them to another item. The 114 million, on the other hand, concern the purchase approved by Parliament in 1993: they are the value of that decision, referring to 180,000 uniforms. The source assigns this amount to the historical purchase and does not describe it as the cost of current disposal.
The reference to 100 million is different again. The Federal Audit Office argued that a better procurement procedure would have made it possible to save up to that amount. The wording describes possible savings linked to planning, not an amount presented as already recovered.
| Period | Reported figure | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | 1993 | 180,000 uniforms for 114 million | purchase approved by Parliament | | 2021 | request for a more modern uniform | initiative by Marianne Binder-Keller | | From 2025 | Dress A only for representational duties | reduction of large-scale distribution | | 26 September 2026 | non-recoverable uniforms sent for incineration | overall number not recorded |
This distinction prevents adding figures that belong to different periods. It also prevents turning the Federal Audit Office's estimate into a reimbursement or into savings already accounted for. The text does not quantify the cost of recycling, indicate how much incineration costs, or provide the number of garments sent to the facilities.
For a reader in Switzerland, the observable point is the handling of an army supply and the transparency of the available data. The connection with one's personal budget remains indirect. Anyone who wants to keep army expenditure separate from their own outlays can use the costo della vita in Svizzera as a comparison tool, without attributing to the military figure effects that the text does not indicate.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## The sequence to follow to verify the data
The source makes it possible to reconstruct a simple procedure for understanding the phase-out without confusing garments, costs and timing. It is also a useful framework for anyone who has to comment on the news or check data reported elsewhere.
### Four steps
1. Identify the period. The only explicit timeline is 2025: from that year onward, Tenuta A is assigned only to military personnel with representational duties. The article is dated 26 settembre 2026. The source does not indicate a final date for the elimination of the gray uniform.
2. Separate use from the condition of the garment. The uniform remains in use for representational duties. For withdrawn uniforms, the operational criterion is the possibility of recovery: garments that can still be used are inspected, repaired and, if necessary, redistributed.
3. Verify the destination. Only uniforms that can no longer be recovered are taken to a waste incineration facility. Saying that all gray uniforms are burned would go beyond what the source reports.
4. Check the figures without conflating them. The 55 milioni di franchi are the overall savings the army intends to achieve by forgoing large-scale distribution. The 114 milioni relate to the 1993 purchase; the 100 milioni are the savings that the Federal Audit Office identified as possible with a better procedure. None of these figures indicates the number of uniforms destined for incineration.
This verification also leads to a practical rule: do not attribute an overall figure to disposal and do not present sale as an available solution. The army rules it out because the uniform is still in use and to avoid the risk of improper use. Recycling, on the other hand, would require making uniforms and insignia unrecognizable and is deemed unreasonable given the costs and work required.

item.description: Popular initiative for parental leave successful with 136'000 signatures. Submission planned at the Federal Chancellery.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- 136’000 signatures collected for parental leave - The signatures will be submitted next week - 100’000 signatures were needed by the first of October - The proposal provides 18 weeks for both parents
## Key facts
- Signatures collected: 136’000 - Initiative: Strong society and economy thanks to parental leave - Promoters: PVL, Verdi, Alliance F, Travail Suisse and Donne del Centro - Required threshold: 100’000 signatures - Collection deadline: first of October - Planned funding: loss-of-earnings compensation insurance - Requested duration: 18 weeks for mothers and fathers - Estimated annual costs: around one billion francs
136’000 signatures have been collected for the popular initiative Strong society and economy thanks to parental leave. The announcement was made by the Green Liberal Party (PVL), one of the promoting forces. The signatures will be submitted next week to the Federal Chancellery. The PVL considers the number sufficient for the initiative to succeed «with a comfortable margin».
The text of the constitutional amendment was published in the Federal Gazette in April 2025. To succeed, the initiative had to collect 100’000 signatures by the first of October. The proposal is promoted, in addition to the PVL, by Verdi, Alliance F, Travail Suisse and Donne del Centro. It is also supported by PS, the Evangelical Party and other organizations.
### The structure of the proposal
The objective is to introduce an adequate and paid congedo parentale for mothers and fathers after the birth of the child. The funding should come through loss-of-earnings compensation insurance. If accepted, the implementing legislation should be ready within five years.
For the first ten years, the text calls for 18 weeks for each parent: in principle, to be taken one after the other, with at most one quarter of the period taken together. The leave would not be transferable from one parent to the other. The amount of the allowance is fundamentally based on the amounts provided for military and civilian service. For lower salaries, however, the initiative provides for an allowance equal to a full salary.
In autumn 2024 Kathrin Bertschy, member of the National Council (PVL/BE) and co-president of the women’s organization Alliance F, had calculated an increase in payroll contributions of 0.25 percentage points, up to 0.75%. According to a study by Ecoplan, the annual costs would be around one billion francs.
Today, working mothers are entitled to a maternity allowance of 14 weeks. In 2020, the Swiss people approved two weeks of paternity leave, introduced at the beginning of 2021. The vote originated from an initiative for four weeks of paternity leave with loss-of-earnings compensation; in Parliament, the indirect counterproposal for two weeks ultimately prevailed. ## Before and after, according to the text
The comparison between the situation described today and the proposed model highlights a different distribution of time after birth. The source indicates 14 weeks of maternity benefits for working mothers and two weeks of paternity leave for fathers, introduced at the beginning of 2021. The initiative instead calls for 18 weeks for each parent within the first ten years.
### Separate planning for each parent
The formula does not provide for a single package to be divided freely. The 18 weeks would apply separately to the mother and father; the basic rule is that they would be taken one after the other, while the overlap could not exceed one quarter of the period. The text also rules out transferring the leave. A family would therefore have to keep the two periods and any shared portion separate when planning. It would not only be the total number of weeks that mattered, but also their order and the shared portion. congedo parentale is thus described as a sequence of coordinated absences, not as a single period that could be freely redistributed.
| Recipient | Current framework indicated | Initiative's request | | Working mothers | 14 weeks of maternity benefits | 18 weeks within the first ten years | | Fathers | 2 weeks of paternity leave | 18 weeks within the first ten years |
The second effect to consider concerns financial coverage. The proposal indicates loss-of-earnings insurance; in autumn 2024 Kathrin Bertschy had calculated an increase in payroll contributions of 0,25 percentage points, with the level indicated at 0,75%. An Ecoplan study estimates the annual costs at approximately one billion francs. The percentage and the cost estimate are therefore the economic elements connected to the initiative proponents' plans, while the structure of the leave defines who could be absent and how the period would be divided.
A practical reading requires keeping these two aspects separate: duration and benefits on the one hand, financing on the other. If the initiative were accepted, the implementing legislation would have to be ready within five years, leaving the legislative text with the task of putting the requested rules into operation.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the initiative
### The practical sequence for the reader
To follow the process without confusing the collection of signatures with the rules governing leave, it is useful to use a checklist based on the steps already indicated:
1. Check the next announced step: the 136’000 signatures will be submitted next week to the Federal Chancellery. This is the immediate operational reference communicated by PVL. 2. Keep the threshold and deadline separate: the proposal required 100’000 signatures, and the deadline indicated for collecting them is the first of October. The announced number and the closing date are the two pieces of data to consider together when reading the initiative. 3. Return to the text published in the Federal Gazette in April 2025 and check four elements: 18 weeks for each parent during the first ten years, in principle taken one after the other, at most one quarter taken together, and no transfer between parents. 4. Separate the duration from the financial calculation: the requested financing would come through loss-of-earnings insurance; the allowance essentially follows the amounts for military and civilian service, while full pay is provided for lower salaries.
This checklist makes it possible to read the proposal in practical terms: first the announced institutional step, then the collection requirements, followed by the rules that would affect the organization of leave, and finally its financing. The text also indicates that, if accepted, the implementing legislation should be ready within five years. For this reason, the stage described in the news report is still that of the initiative’s success and the submission of the signatures; future operational arrangements depend on the legislation provided for in the text.
For anyone planning a birth, the useful comparison is between the framework currently indicated for mothers and fathers and the structure requested by the initiative, without treating the proposal as a rule already in force. The estimates of wage contributions and annual costs, on the other hand, are useful for assessing the financial side of the project. To explore congedo parentale further, you can consider the document, timeline and rules together; to translate the effect of the contributions indicated by the promoters on personal income, open calcolatore stipendio.

item.description: In mid-2026, Switzerland ranks 16th in Europe for the electrification of cars. One quarter of new registrations are electric.

## In brief - Switzerland is in 16th place in mid-2026. - Electric vehicles account for a quarter of new registrations. - In August, the electric share reached 30%. - In some places, an electric SUV costs up to 1000 francs more per year.
## Key facts - Interviewee → Helmut Ruhl, CEO of Amag - Location → Aarau - European ranking → fifth in 2019; 13th at the end of 2025; 16th in mid-2026 - Share this year → a quarter of new registrations - August → 30% of new registrations were purely electric - Tax difference → up to 1000 francs more per year for an average electric SUV - Survey → 84% of Swiss people prefer German car manufacturers
AARAU – In mid-2026, Switzerland fell to 16th place in the European comparison of vehicle electrification. This is the view of Helmut Ruhl, CEO of importer Amag, in an interview published by Aargauer Zeitung. In 2019, the country was in fifth place; at the end of 2025, it was 13th. The sequence shows a relative decline: the market is progressing, but more slowly than many other European countries.
The paradox highlighted by the manager is the rise in gasoline prices while Switzerland remains a stronghold of the combustion engine. According to Ruhl, a quarter of new registrations this year concern purely electric cars. In August, the share reached 30%, and in September it was even higher. High fuel prices, says the importer of the Volkswagen, Audi, Skoda, Seat and Cupra brands, are contributing to additional demand.
### Conditions holding things back
In Ruhl’s view, the barriers instead lie in the framework conditions, which he defines as contradictory. Many people live in rented accommodation or in condominiums without having the right to a charging option. Public parking facilities also lack infrastructure. The cantons also apply different incentives regarding motor vehicle taxes. In some places, a mid-range electric SUV ends up costing up to 1000 francs more per year in taxes than a comparable gasoline-powered car.
According to the interviewee, electric mobility has nevertheless gained momentum recently. The shift from gasoline to electric is thus caught between growing demand and conditions that remain uneven.
> «This cannot be», Ruhl concludes.
For those living in Switzerland, the comparison therefore concerns not only the price of gasoline: it includes available charging and the annual burden of vehicle taxes. These are items to consider also in costo della vita in Svizzera. ## The comparison that varies from canton to canton
For those living in Switzerland, the choice of an electric car is based on three separate checks. The first concerns charging. For those who live in rented accommodation or a condominium, the absence of a right to charge can make the availability of public parking spaces decisive. If the infrastructure is lacking there too, the price of gasoline is not the only factor in the decision: the practical possibility of using the car every day also matters.
### Charging, taxes and brand
The second check is the motor vehicle tax. Ruhl points out that the Cantons apply different incentives. The comparison must be made between vehicles in the same segment and based on annual expenditure: in some places, a mid-range electric SUV can cost up to 1000 francs more in taxes than a comparable gasoline car. This figure describes an annual difference and not the vehicle's purchase price.
| Item | Indication from the source | |---|---| | Fuel prices | Rising | | Vehicle tax | Different incentives among the Cantons | | Mid-range electric SUV | Up to 1000 francs more per year in some places | | Charging | Right absent in many cases; inadequate infrastructure in public parking spaces |
The third element is the brand. Chinese competition is growing, but Ruhl believes that European manufacturers are well positioned. The survey cited in the interview indicates that 84% of Swiss people prefer German car manufacturers for electric cars as well. For consumers, this figure should be read as an indicator of preference, not as a ranking of models.
The discussion also has an industrial dimension. Ruhl argues that Europe must reconcile climate protection with the competitiveness of the automotive industry. He supports tariffs and local production requirements as a response to what he considers unequal competitive conditions with Beijing. He recalls that China has already worked with tariffs, local production obligations and joint ventures. His proposal concerns European industrial policy and should be kept distinct from the comparison between the annual tax on an electric car and that on a gasoline car. To turn the elements of the interview into a concrete choice, it is advisable to follow a simple sequence. The order helps avoid starting from the price of gasoline alone and separate local conditions from brand preferences.
### Five checks before choosing
1. Start with the residence. Indicate whether the parking space is associated with a rented accommodation or a property divided into floors. The source notes that many people in these circumstances are not entitled to a charging option. The first check is therefore actual access to charging.
2. Check public parking. If private charging is unavailable, check the infrastructure at the public parking facility used. The source points out that the infrastructure is lacking there too.
3. Compare the vehicle tax. Collect the figure applied by the Canton and compare a mid-range electric SUV with a comparable gasoline car. In some places, the difference reaches 1000 francs per year to the disadvantage of the electric vehicle. Do not extend this amount to all Cantons: the point is the variety of incentives.
4. Note the market trend. Use the quarter of new electric registrations in the current year, the 30% in August and the even higher September figure as separate indicators. You can set these milestones alongside fifth place in 2019, 13th at the end of 2025 and 16th in mid-2026.
5. Assess the brand and keep the issues separate. The 84% found in the survey concerns the preference for German manufacturers. The proposal for tariffs and local-production requirements, by contrast, concerns Ruhl's position on Europe and competition with Beijing.
The final result must keep available charging, the cantonal tax, comparison between comparable vehicles and demand trends distinct. To translate these items into a personal budget, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Health insurance premiums: the net burden remained stable
item.description: NZZ analysis of 300'000 families: between 2016 and 2023, the net burden of premiums remained stable thanks to subsidies and income growth.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 2027 premiums expected to grow between 4% and 5% - Net burden: 6.5% in 2016 and 6.4% in 2023 - Standard premium: +19% between 2016 and 2023 - Median family: income from 88,875 to 95,760 francs
## Key facts - Period → from 2016 to 2023 - Sample → approximately 300,000 families across Switzerland - Analysis → ten income categories - Data → Helsana insured persons and anonymized official income data - Assessment → net burden after state subsidies
Next week, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider will announce the average growth of health insurance premiums expected for 2027. The expected increase is between 4% and 5%. The NZZ considers the interpretation of a generalized «blow» to be excessive. The topic directly concerns spending on health insurance, but the analysis primarily measures the actual weight after subsidies.
## The comparison between premiums, income, and subsidies
Economists Stefan Felder, Stefan Meyer, and Kurt Schmidheiny from the Basel Center for Health Economics analyzed information from all Helsana insured persons. The data were cross-referenced in anonymized form with official income data. For the NZZ, the group carried out a special assessment of approximately 300,000 families across Switzerland, divided into ten categories, from the lowest to the highest decile.
The result concerns the net burden of health insurance bills after the deduction of state subsidies. Between 2016 and 2023, it remained stable across all income brackets. For a middle-class family, the share of gross income allocated to premiums was 6.5% in 2016 and fell to 6.4% in 2023.
This figure should be compared with the standard premium, defined by the source as that with the lowest deductible and free choice of doctor. That premium grew by 19% over the same period. However, the gross premiums for the median family increased by 11%, equivalent to 750 francs more per year. The median gross income rose from 88,875 francs in 2016 to 95,760 in 2023: the increase of 6,885 francs more than covered the increase in premiums.
### The role of public support
A third element is represented by federal and cantonal subsidies, which rose by approximately 440 francs for the median family. More than half of the premium growth was therefore absorbed by the Confederation and the cantons. The NZZ also notes that in 2023, families with children paid on average no more than 8% of their gross income. In the lowest decile, without state support, the burden would exceed 20%; however, for many households, social support fully covers the premiums and reduces the share to less than 5%. ## National figures do not erase local differences
Average stability does not mean that every household has experienced the same evolution. The same analysis points to marked regional differences: premiums are higher in Ticino, in some regions of Romandie, and in Basel. In these areas, there are families with a net burden exceeding 10% of their gross income. In the rest of Switzerland, according to the NZZ conclusion, the weight of premiums has remained sustainable for the population, despite numerous complaints.
For the reader, the correct comparison involves three levels: gross premium, subsidy, and gross income. The standard premium is not enough to describe the actual expenditure, because many insured persons have switched to models with limited choice of doctor or higher deductibles. The net figure, on the other hand, incorporates public support. This explains why a nominal increase in the premium does not automatically translate into an equivalent growth in the share of income committed.
### A family budget item to be read separately
The comparison concerns LAMal/KVG premiums and the cost of living in Switzerland, not other budget items. Mandatory health insurance premiums are distinct from direct federal tax, VAT, AVS/AHV, and LPP/BVG; in the snapshot examined by the NZZ, support comes from federal and cantonal subsidies. This distinction serves to avoid confusing a per capita bill with salary contributions or a tax. The Cantons matter because the analysis explicitly identifies the role of cantonal subsidies and regional differences.
The most delicate part concerns the recent period. Since 2024, premiums have grown more rapidly: the overall progression from 2024 to 2026 is similar to that recorded from 2016 to 2023, while incomes have only increased on average. The NZZ therefore admits that the burden may have become heavier. Linking subsidies to reference premiums should have covered a substantial part of the increases, but only future data will reveal how much the burden has actually grown.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## From national data to personal assessment
To turn the analysis into a personal assessment, it is useful to work with three values: gross premium, subsidy and gross income. The first step is to keep them separate. The amount to compare with income is not the isolated gross bill, but what remains after public support. This distinction makes it possible to assess the actual burden without confusing the increase in the premium with the increase in expenditure borne by the family.
### A five-step sequence
1. At the time of the announcement scheduled for next week, note the average growth in premiums for 2027 and use it as a general reference, not as a substitute for the data concerning your household. 2. Report the gross premium and the state subsidy separately, so that you can reconstruct the net burden. 3. Indicate the insurance model observed: the standard premium corresponds to the lowest deductible and the free choice of doctor; the other models may provide for limited choice and higher deductibles. 4. Compare the net amount with the household's gross income and note the year, so that you can distinguish a change in income from one in premiums. 5. Read the result on two levels: the national and the regional. The analysis in fact separates the Swiss average from the areas where the net burden is higher.
For the period from 2024 to 2026, keep the comparison provisional. The progression of premiums was faster and incomes grew only on average; the role of subsidies, linked to reference premiums, will have to be measured using future data. The analysis itself defers the definitive assessment until this information becomes available.
When Baume-Schneider announces the average growth for 2027, update the comparison with the amount actually paid and the subsidy received. To relate income to the personal budget, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Hail insurance: compensation up to 170 million
item.description: Grandine Svizzera expects compensation payments of up to 170 million francs in 2026. Adrian Aebi warns: premiums could become unaffordable.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Compensation of up to 170 million francs expected in 2026 - Aebi fears premiums will be difficult for many companies to afford - Sugar beets, potatoes and maize: yields up to 30% lower - Investments are needed to adapt to climate change
## Key facts - Location → Zurich - Interviewee → Adrian Aebi - Organization → Grandine Svizzera - Compensation in 2026 → up to 170 million francs - Yield losses → up to 30% - Branches → France, Italy and Liechtenstein
In 2026 Grandine Svizzera expects to have to pay the agricultural sector compensation of up to 170 million francs. The cooperative, which offers insurance coverage for agricultural crops, is preparing for a huge financial loss. The warning was issued by Adrian Aebi, director of Grandine Svizzera, in an interview with the Neue Zürcher Zeitung.
### The threshold indicated by the director
Aebi distinguishes between a single unfavorable year and a sequence of damaging years. An insurer, he explains, can cope with an isolated poor result. The pressure changes if the same type of year recurs at short intervals.
> «if such a damaging year were to occur every three years in the future, the situation would become difficult»
According to the director, crop losses will in principle remain insurable. The issue concerns the price of coverage: if damage continues to increase, premiums could reach levels that would be difficult for many farms to sustain.
The source already points to an unfavorable combination for the sector. Farmers have to contend with higher irrigation and labor costs, while yields are lower. In 2026, spring-sown crops, including sugar beets, potatoes and maize, recorded yield losses of up to 30% in some cases.
For Aebi, the response involves two levers: higher prices for agricultural products and investments in adapting to climate change. The measures mentioned include more drought-resistant varieties, higher-quality soils and more efficient irrigation systems. Without adjustments and higher revenues, many farms could struggle to sustain rising costs and risks over the long term.
The Società Svizzera di Assicurazione contro la Grandine is among the leading European companies in multirisk insurance for agriculture. Through its branches, it also insures crops in France, Italy and Liechtenstein. ## What it means for companies' accounts
The practical reading of the case begins with a distinction: the risk does not end with compensation after the damage. If irrigation and labor costs rise together, yields decline and premiums increase, the company's financial stability comes under multiple pressures. The source therefore describes an overall sustainability problem, not merely an insurance coverage issue.
| Scenario | Effect to consider | |---|---| | An isolated unfavorable year | The insurer may be able to cope with it. | | A damaging year every three years | The situation becomes difficult. | | Increasing damage | Premiums may become difficult for many companies to sustain. |
The comparison helps show where the threshold shifts. In principle, losses remain insurable; the difficulty arises when the cost of protection is added to already higher business costs and lower yields. For an agricultural business, the question is not merely whether coverage exists, but whether its price remains compatible with revenues.
### Adaptation and revenues
The measures indicated by Aebi can be understood as three directions for investment.
| Measure indicated | Objective stated in the source | |---|---| | Varieties more resistant to drought | Adapt to drought. | | Higher-quality land | Improve the production base. | | More efficient irrigation systems | Make irrigation more efficient. |
Alongside these choices, the director calls for higher prices for agricultural products. The text presents this indication as a condition for achieving higher revenues, not as an increase in prices that has already been decided. For those living in Switzerland, the distinction is useful: the source does not announce a price increase for consumers, but points to pressure on the sector's finances. The overall picture can be followed through the costo della vita in Svizzera.
Labor is cited as a cost for companies, without any change in individual remuneration. To separate the agricultural balance sheet from the worker's situation, one can consult the guide to the busta paga svizzera.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A practical path for reading risk
2026 is the concrete time reference provided by the source. A Swiss farm can use that year to turn the alarm into an orderly assessment, without attributing the same result to all crops or all farms.
### Steps to line up
1. **Define the scope.** Identify the crops sown in spring and separate sugar beets, potatoes and corn. The yield loss of up to 30% is attributed by the source only to certain cases: it should not be treated as a general average.
2. Separate the items. Compare irrigation expenses, labor costs, yields obtained and insurance premiums. The assessment serves to distinguish agricultural damage from the cost necessary to produce and protect oneself.
3. Test two scenarios. First assess the effect of a single unfavorable year and then that of a damaging year recurring every three years. These are the two situations referred to by Aebi; the comparison makes it possible to understand when coverage risks becoming difficult to sustain.
4. Prioritize investments. Examine the three solutions indicated: varieties more resistant to drought, higher-quality land and more efficient irrigation systems. The choice should be linked to the pressure weighing most heavily on the farm's accounts.
5. Verify revenues. Consider the request for higher agricultural prices together with rising costs and risks. The source does not indicate a precise price: the operational point is to measure what level of revenues is needed to sustain the activity in the long term.
This path avoids two misreadings. The 170 million francs are compensation expected for the sector, not a sum allocated to every farm. Likewise, 30% indicates yield losses recorded in certain cases, not the result for all crops sown in spring.
For the personal budget of someone working in Switzerland, the final step is to estimate the available margin with the calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.description: Federal Councillor Beat Jans focuses on European cooperation and fast-track return procedures during the Munich summit with 18 states.

## In brief
- Switzerland is aiming for stronger European cooperation - Switzerland intends to intensify the cross-border fight - Summit in Munich with ministers from 18 European states - Five countries promote the «Return Hubs»
## Key facts
- Who → Beat Jans, Federal Councillor - Where → Munich - Participants → ministers from 18 European states and the European Commission - Pact → entered into force on 12 June - Return Hubs → Denmark, Greece, the Netherlands, Austria and Germany
### Switzerland's position at the summit
Federal Councillor Beat Jans attended an immigration summit in Munich, convened at the invitation of German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt. Ministers from 18 European states and representatives of the European Commission were present. The United Kingdom was present; Spain was absent and France did not join the meeting.
Jans indicated the need for swift and efficient European procedures, effective transfers under the Dublin Regulation and consistent enforcement of removal orders. Switzerland intends to intensify the cross-border fight against human traffickers, while respecting international law and human rights, the FDJP said.
The talks concerned the European Pact on Migration and Asylum, which entered into force on 12 June, return policy and cooperation within the Schengen area. The FDJP says that Switzerland is fulfilling its obligations and expects the same from its partners; initial experiences with the new procedures are overall positive.
According to the department, a credible migration policy strengthens Schengen as an area of freedom, security and justice. Switzerland, described in the statement as a highly interconnected country, wants to preserve and develop this area by deepening cooperation with neighboring countries and at European level against transnational crime, traffickers and trafficking networks.
The statement does not quantify effects on incomes or household spending. For a separate in-depth look at costo della vita in Svizzera, the topic should be kept distinct from the migration policy described in Munich.
### Frontex and return centers
The summit also addressed surveillance of the EU's external borders and the strengthening of Frontex. The Commission is preparing changes: today the agency supports member states with expulsions, but responsibility remains with national authorities. The agency should be given a stronger mandate to cooperate with non-EU countries and a greater role in returns.
The CEAS allows centers in third countries for people who have no right to remain in the EU and are subject to return. The «Return Hubs» are promoted by Denmark, Greece, the Netherlands, Austria and Germany. Destinations mentioned include Rwanda, Uganda and Uzbekistan; the agreements are intended to be finalized by the end of the year. The source notes concerns expressed by international organizations about respect for human rights in Rwanda. ## From the summit to discernible implications
In the text provided, the announcement concerns a direction for cooperation, not an individual procedure. It does not indicate documents to submit, amounts or deadlines for Swiss residents. The national link is institutional: the DFGP links migration management to the defence and development of Schengen, while Switzerland declares that it wants to work with neighbouring countries and European partners.
### Three operational levels
The first level is Swiss: the country fulfils its obligations and wants to intensify the cross-border fight against traffickers. The second is European: the Pact on Migration and Asylum, returns, external borders and Schengen. The third concerns implementation: national authorities remain in principle responsible for expulsions, while Frontex provides support and could receive a broader mandate.
| Topic | Situation described | Development indicated | |---|---|---| | Dublin | Functioning transfers are needed | Fast and efficient procedures | | Frontex | Support for expulsions; national responsibility | Cooperation with non-EU countries and more returns | | Return Hubs | Possible centres in third countries according to the CEAS | Agreements promoted by five states by the end of the year |
The distinction between the present and the outlook is decisive. The Pact entered into force on 12 June and Switzerland's first experiences with the new procedures are overall positive. Changes to Frontex, on the other hand, are being prepared by the European Commission. The agreements on «Return Hubs» are also an objective of the five promoting states: the source does not present them as already concluded.
For residents, the practical message is limited but concrete: the communiqué places Switzerland within a European network of procedures, returns and cooperation against transnational crime. It does not describe new border rules for individuals, nor a specific administrative procedure. To separate this aspect from the employment dimension, the annunci di lavoro can be consulted, without presenting them as an announced effect of the summit.
### The point of attention
The follow-up will be measured against three elements indicated in the source: the functioning of Dublin transfers, Frontex's future mandate and the possible conclusion of agreements with third countries by the end of the year. The reference to rights is not incidental: the DFGP cites international law and human rights, while the Rwanda case is accompanied by doubts expressed by international organizations.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the developments without confusing the announcements
To read future updates in an orderly manner, it is advisable to separate what Switzerland has communicated from what Europe is still preparing. The following sequence uses only the steps indicated in the source.
1. Identify the level. If the update concerns the cross-border fight against traffickers, the reference is the Swiss position communicated by the FDFA. If it concerns Frontex, ASYLUM, or the «Return Hubs», the reference is the European framework and cooperation with third countries.
2. Verify the status. The European Pact on Migration and Asylum entered into force on June 12. According to the FDFA, the new procedures have produced overall positive initial experiences. Changes to Frontex, on the other hand, are currently being prepared.
3. Check the responsibility. In deportations, Frontex supports Member States, but responsibility generally lies with the national authorities. This is the criterion for distinguishing agency support from a decision by national authorities.
4. Note the political deadline. Agreements with third countries for the «Return Hubs» aim for closure by the end of the year. The five promoting states are Denmark, Greece, the Netherlands, Austria, and Germany; among the mentioned countries are Rwanda, Uganda, and Uzbekistan.
5. Verify the legal constraints. Every development must be read alongside the FDFA's reference to international law and human rights. The source also notes the doubts of international organizations regarding the respect for human rights in Rwanda.
### A checklist
For every new press release, note four items: who is speaking, which geographical area is involved, which measure is being described, and at what stage it is. The institutions named in the text are the FDFA, the European Commission, Frontex, and national authorities. The areas are Switzerland, neighboring countries, the European Union, and third countries. The measures concern procedures, repatriations, external borders, or cooperation against traffickers.
This checklist prevents a project from being mistaken for a rule already in application. The source does not provide amounts, documents, or personal administrative instructions for Swiss residents; the reader can therefore first verify whether the update describes a fact already in force, operational support, a change in preparation, or an agreement yet to be closed.

item.description: Decision of 25 September 2026 to harmonize financial provisions on terrorism and proliferation, with specific exemptions for Iran.

## In brief - 25 September 2026: Federal Council decision - Four ordinances on financial sanctions - UN: terrorism and weapons of mass destruction - Iran: exemption extended to international organizations
## Key facts - Date → 25 September 2026 - Place → Bern - Decision → standardize and clarify the financial provisions - Scope → four sanctions ordinances - Basis → UN sanctions on terrorism and proliferation - Precedent → 13 August 2025 - Iran update → exemption for international organizations and certain transactions
On 25 September 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council decided to standardize and clarify the financial provisions contained in four ordinances implementing UN sanctions relating to the financing of terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. The decision therefore concerns a defined set of financial rules linked to sanction measures.
### The four ordinances concerned
The first text concerns the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and the second the Islamic Republic of Iran. The other two concern persons, groups, companies and entities linked to the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda organizations, as well as persons and groups linked to the Taliban. The Federal Council indicated the same intervention for all four: clarifying and harmonizing the financial provisions.
The ordinances implement, in particular, the sanctions of the United Nations Security Council on the financing of terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. The press release thus links the amendment to the sanctions of the United Nations Security Council.
### The exemption provided for Iran
The most narrowly defined development concerns the ordinance establishing measures against the Islamic Republic of Iran. From now on, international organizations will benefit from an exemption from notification and authorization requirements for certain transactions. The same development is also described as extending to international organizations the exemptions from notification and authorization requirements for transfers of assets provided for by the ordinance.
The source does not list the transactions concerned in this press release and does not indicate any amounts. To correctly understand the practical effect, the starting point therefore remains the distinction between the ordinance on Iran and the other three. For banking topics not connected to the sanctions regime, the site offers a guide to conti bancari in Svizzera.
### The 2025 step
The changes of 25 September 2026 correspond to the clarifications and harmonizations introduced by the Federal Council on 13 August 2025 in the respective ordinances, which at that time were based on European Union sanctions. With the new legislative act, the Federal Council now emphasizes the financial measures based on the resolutions of the United Nations Security Council. The date and the dual reference — European Union and UN — define the regulatory trajectory described in the press release. ### What changes for interpreting the rules
For those who must assess a financial transaction falling under one of the four ordinances, the novelty is not a monetary threshold, because the communiqué does not specify one. The practical point is the uniform rewriting of the financial provisions and, for Iran, the extension of an exemption to a specific category: international organizations.
For an activity in Switzerland, the distinction is concrete: the harmonization concerns the wording of the financial provisions, while the Iranian exemption is linked to the category of the entity and the nature of the transaction.
Before the act of 25 September 2026, the source described exemptions for asset transfers in the ordinance on Iran, but did not present them as extended to international organizations. Following the decision, these organizations benefit from the exemption for certain transactions. However, the wording does not authorize turning the novelty into a general exemption: the text retains the reference both to the specified transactions and to the Iranian ordinance.
For the ordinances concerning the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, persons and entities linked to ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda, and persons and groups linked to the Taliban, the communiqué speaks of clarification and harmonization of the financial provisions. It does not attribute to these three areas the extension of the exemption provided for Iran. This distinction avoids applying the novelty mechanically to all measures.
### Two sanctions bases to keep separate
The comparison with 13 August 2025 adds a second level of interpretation. The clarifications and harmonizations of 2025 were based on European Union sanctions; the act of 25 September 2026 emphasizes financial measures based on resolutions of the United Nations Security Council. Anyone analyzing the text must therefore verify which ordinance they are consulting and which sanctions basis is invoked, without confusing the two stages.
The communiqué does not provide a list of documents, offices, forms or deadlines for notifications and authorizations. Consequently, everyday exchange-rate tools do not replace the regulatory text: comparatore CHF/EUR is used for currency comparison, not to determine whether a transaction benefits from the exemption. ### A five-step verification
The process can begin with the PDF made available together with the press release, entitled Ordinance concerning the amendment of ordinances on sanctions in relation to proliferation and terrorist financing. The verification must remain anchored in the text of the ordinances, because the source announces the principle of the amendment but does not provide the list of transactions concerned.
1. Identify the relevant ordinance. The first step is to distinguish between the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the persons, groups, companies and entities linked to ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda, as well as the persons and groups linked to the Taliban. This classification prevents a rule from one text being automatically transferred to another.
2. Isolate the financial aspect. The decision concerns financial provisions; it is therefore necessary to read the passage relating to notification, authorization or transfers of assets, when the applicable ordinance refers to them.
3. If the reference is Iran, check the two conditions described in the press release: the transaction must fall among those specified and the entity must be an international organization in order to assess the announced exemption.
4. Verify the basis of the measure. The text must be read while keeping distinct the previous clarification of 13 agosto 2025, based on European Union sanctions, from the emphasis placed on 25 settembre 2026 on the resolutions of the United Nations Security Council.
5. Retain the correct reference. The document indicated in the source is the Ordinance concerning the amendment of ordinances on sanctions in relation to proliferation and terrorist financing, published on 25 settembre 2026. This is the reference to use to compare the announced wording with the applicable provisions.
The press release does not indicate an online procedure, a recipient authority, a form or an operational deadline. It is therefore not possible to derive a more detailed administrative process from this text without adding information extraneous to the source. The concrete verification must stop at the criteria explicitly described: ordinance, type of transaction, nature of the organization and obligation concerned.

item.title: Ubs: relocation of headquarters unlikely, according to Keller-Sutter
item.description: According to Karin Keller‑Sutter, moving Ubs’s headquarters abroad would be much more costly and legally complex; the Federal Council has already granted concessions regarding the Capital Adequacy Ordinance.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Keller-Sutter considers the relocation of Ubs's headquarters abroad unlikely - Ubs contests the proposals on capital requirements - The orientation in the Council of States was different - A meeting with Colm Kelleher is scheduled for November
## Key facts - Main figure: Karin Keller-Sutter - Bank: Ubs - Dossier: stricter rules on own funds - Institution: Federal Council - Recent decision: Council of States - CEO mentioned: Sergio Ermotti - Chairman of the board mentioned: Colm Kelleher - Interview: Aargauer Zeitung
A relocation of Ubs's headquarters abroad, considered in connection with the planned stricter rules on own funds, appears unlikely according to Karin Keller-Sutter. The finance minister said this in an interview published by Aargauer Zeitung. The point of her argument is the relationship between the capital requirements being discussed at federal level and the cost of any relocation.
### The concessions already granted
Keller-Sutter recalls that the Federal Council granted Ubs significant concessions under the own-funds ordinance.
> “We granted Ubs significant concessions under the own-funds ordinance.”
The Federal Council also refrained from further general tightening of capital ratios, recommended by experts after the Credit Suisse crisis. Despite these decisions, Ubs called all the minister's proposals “extreme”. Keller-Sutter describes the institution's approach as an aggressive strategy, probably based on the idea that it would prevail in Parliament anyway, as had happened in the past.
The minister presents these measures as an element that makes the possibility of a relocation less plausible. Her account therefore concerns both own funds and the relationship between Ubs and its Swiss headquarters: not only the rules applicable to the institution, but also the cost and complexity of leaving.
### The political response
The recent decision by the Council of States, however, showed a different orientation, at least in that chamber. According to the minister, Ubs must not leave the Confederation: many analysts and experts consider the requirements reasonable and easily manageable for the institution.
A relocation would be much more expensive and legally very complex, Keller-Sutter adds. The bank would no longer be Swiss, while its business model is based on Switzerland, on “Swissness”, on the rule of law and on the country's political stability. The Federal Councillor also points to private banks and capital inflows recorded during the conflict in the Middle East: for her, these are signs of confidence in Switzerland as an operating base.
The dossier remains in Parliament. After the Council of States' decision, Keller-Sutter did not call CEO Sergio Ermotti, and the CEO did not get in touch. A meeting with Ubs chairman Colm Kelleher is scheduled for November, during a regular exchange of views with representatives of the financial centre. The minister specifies, however, that this is not the time to negotiate.
To find one's way around Swiss banking services, readers can consult the guide to conti bancari in Svizzera. ### What changes for people living in Switzerland
The news should be read as an institutional development, not as an operational order addressed to residents. The source does not announce a transfer that has already taken place, a closure, or new conditions for customers: it reports Keller-Sutter's assessment that leaving the Confederation would be more costly and legally complex. For the national public, the concrete point is therefore the scope of the comparison: equity capital, the bank's headquarters, and its relationship with Switzerland.
The first practical distinction concerns the political timetable. The relief measures in the ordinance on capital requirements and the decision to forgo further general tightening are already presented by the minister as decisions that have been adopted; the dossier on stricter rules remains under review by Parliament. The reader must not confuse a contested proposal with a rule already in force.
| Element to keep separate | Practical reading | |---|---| | Relief measures granted | Keller-Sutter's stated starting point. | | Further tightening | The Federal Council has generally decided against it. | | Requirements under discussion | The analysts and experts cited consider them reasonable and manageable. | | Swiss headquarters | The minister links it to «swissness», the rule of law, and political stability. |
This comparison has an interpretive consequence: Ubs's possible departure is not described as an automatic response to a single act, but as a choice that would entail costs and complexities of its own. Keller-Sutter adds that, outside Switzerland, the bank would no longer be a Swiss bank. For those who work or live in the country, the reference to «swissness» signals the value the minister attaches to the headquarters, but does not provide an estimate of employment, incomes, or daily spending.

item.title: Health insurance premiums rise, but the burden on families remains stable
item.description: From 2016 to 2023, the net burden on households remained stable: the standard premium increased by 19%, but its share of average income fell from 6,5% to 6,4% thanks to an increase in subsidies of approximately 440 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - From 2016 to 2023, the net burden remained stable - In 2027, expected premiums will rise by between 4% and 5% - The middle class goes from 6.5% to 6.4% of gross income - The standard premium rose by 19%
## Key facts
| Term | Value | |---|---| | Period analyzed | 2016-2023 | | Sample | approximately 300'000 families | | Data source | Helsana policyholders and anonymized official income data | | Income categories | ten | | Median gross income in 2016 | 88'875 francs | | Median gross income in 2023 | 95'760 francs | | Standard premium | +19% from 2016 to 2023 | | Subsidies for the median family | approximately 440 francs more |
## The central finding of the analysis
From Zurich, the Neue Zürcher Zeitung relaunches the findings of a special assessment based on a study by the University of Basel. The conclusion concerns an issue felt throughout Switzerland: despite the increase in premiums, the net burden borne by families has remained essentially stable in recent years.
### How the burden was calculated
The economists Stefan Felder, Stefan Meyer and Kurt Schmidheiny, from the Basel Center for Health Economics, analyzed information on all Helsana policyholders. The data were cross-referenced in anonymized form with official income information. For the NZZ, the group then prepared an assessment of approximately 300'000 families distributed throughout Switzerland, examining the period from 2016 to 2023 and dividing households into ten income categories.
The result concerns bills net of state subsidies. In all income brackets, the burden remained stable. For a middle-class family, the share of gross income allocated to premiums fell from 6.5% in 2016 to 6.4% in 2023, even though the standard premium, calculated using the lowest deductible and free choice of doctor, increased by 19%.
The NZZ identifies three factors. Many policyholders chose models with limited choice of doctor and higher deductibles, reducing payments. For the median family, gross premiums grew by 11%, i.e. by 750 francs a year. In the meantime, median gross income rose from 88'875 francs to 95'760, an increase of 6885 francs. Federal and cantonal subsidies rose by approximately 440 francs for the median family. More than half of the increase in premiums was therefore absorbed by the Confederation and the cantons.
The analysis also considers families with children, who in 2023 paid on average no more than 8% of gross income. Without state support, for the lowest decile the burden would exceed 20%; with social support, which for many households covers premiums in full, it falls to less than 5%.
Next week, the NZZ recalls, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider will announce the average premium increase for 2027, expected to be between 4% and 5%. ### The relationship between premiums and income
The comparison suggested by the analysis is between the gross bill, gross income and the share that remains after subsidies. Looking only at the standard premium can therefore offer a different picture from the one that emerges for the household budget. The median family illustrates this gap well: the price of the standard model increased, but the net burden relative to income remained almost unchanged.
| Indicator | Trend identified | |---|---| | Median gross income | from 88'875 to 95'760 francs | | Burden for the middle class | from 6.5% to 6.4% | | Standard premium | +19% | | Gross premiums for the median family | +11%, equal to 750 francs annually | | Federal and cantonal subsidies | around 440 francs more |
This difference matters especially when comparing different years. An increase in the bill does not automatically produce the same increase in the burden if income or subsidies grow in the meantime. The study also indicates that switching to plans with more limited choice of doctor and higher deductibles reduced payments for many policyholders. This does not mean that every family followed the same path, but it explains why the standard premium alone does not describe actual spending.
For families with children, the 2023 average does not exceed 8% of gross income. The situation of lower incomes is, however, more sensitive to aid: without state support, the burden of the lowest decile would exceed 20%; for many households, social assistance fully covers the premiums and brings the burden below 5%. The result therefore shows a redistributive effect of subsidies, not a uniform reduction in bills.
The region also changes the interpretation. In Ticino, in some regions of Romandy and in Basel, premiums are higher and some families exceed a net burden of 10% of gross income. The national average does not erase these differences. To compare the insurance figure with the household's other expenses, one can consult costo della vita in Svizzera.

NZZ therefore acknowledges that the burden may have become heavier, but also observes that linking subsidies to reference premiums should have left the state covering a substantial part of the increases. In 2019, Switzerland ranked fifth in Europe for vehicle electrification. At the end of 2025, it was in 13th place; in mid-2026, it had dropped to 16th. This sequence was cited by Helmut Ruhl, CEO of Amag, in an interview published by Aargauer Zeitung.
The manager summarized the situation as follows: «We are progressing faster than before, but more slowly than many other European countries». Switzerland remains a stronghold of the combustion engine, despite rising petrol prices.
### The framework conditions indicated by Amag
According to Ruhl, the delay stems from contradictory framework conditions. Many people live in rented accommodation or in condominiums, but do not have access to a charging option. The problem also affects public spaces: public car parks lack infrastructure.
A second reason concerns motor vehicle taxes. The cantons apply different incentives and, in some places, a mid-range electric SUV costs up to 1'000 francs more per year in taxes than a comparable petrol car. Ruhl considers this difference unacceptable.
However, the demand picture is less negative than the ranking. According to the interviewee, electric mobility has recently gained momentum: in the current year, purely electric cars account for one quarter of new registrations. In August, the share was 30%, and in September it was even slightly higher. High fuel prices are also contributing to additional demand, says the importer of the Volkswagen, Audi, Skoda, Seat and Cupra brands.
Growing Chinese competition remains a factor. Ruhl believes that European manufacturers are still well positioned. The overall picture is therefore mixed: electric demand is accelerating, but the country is falling behind in the European comparison and continues to face obstacles related to charging and taxes. ## The comparison that changes with the canton

item.description: MOBILO 26 involved approximately 3'000 soldiers, 300 wheeled vehicles and 50 armored vehicles from Bière to Frauenfeld, with a floating bridge.

## In brief - MOBILO 26 involved approximately 3'000 soldiers - 300 kilometers from Bière (VD) to Frauenfeld (TG) - Pontoon Battalion 26 assembled a floating bridge - Artillery Group 49 moved in less than 72 hours
## Key facts - Exercise → MOBILO 26 - Conclusion → Friday - Personnel → approximately 3'000 soldiers - Equipment → 300 wheeled vehicles and 50 armored vehicles - Motto → be ready in 24 hours - Route → Bière (VD)-Frauenfeld (TG) - Bridge → Pontoon Battalion 26 - Reconnaissance → ADS 15 drone
### A test in the field
Approximately 3'000 soldiers, 300 wheeled vehicles and 50 armored vehicles participated in MOBILO 26, the exercise with which the Swiss Armed Forces tested their capacity for rapid mobilization. The movement covered approximately 300 kilometers, from Bière (VD) to Frauenfeld (TG), and concluded on Friday.
The operation's motto was to be ready in 24 hours. To achieve this, the movements took place mainly at night and discreetly. The source gives two reasons: tactical considerations and the desire to avoid unnecessary displays of force. Speed was tested together with the ability to move personnel and equipment without making the operation more visible than necessary.
Cooperation between units had a concrete component. Pontoon Battalion 26 assembled a floating bridge to cross a waterway; the first elements of Artillery Group 49 crossed it. This was not a simulation in the field: Artillery Group 49 entered service on Monday and less than 72 hours later was already moving with its vehicles.
Preparation required anticipating weather conditions, planning the assembly of the bridge and coordinating the arrival of the vehicles. The exercise also included mobile communication systems, medical and logistical equipment, and air defense systems. The ADS 15 reconnaissance drone provided information for the safety of the movements.
The commander of the Land Forces, Divisionary Yves Gächter, and his staff tested the procedures under realistic conditions. The route crossed Vaud's Lake Geneva arc, the Fribourg Plateau, the Seeland, the southern foothills of the Solothurn Jura, the Emmental and Upper Aargau. For readers also following the work dossier, the site places this report alongside the guide to busta paga svizzera. ## Speed Depends on the Operational Chain
### Five Elements to Read Together
The exercise shows that rapid mobilization does not coincide solely with vehicle speed. In the exercise material, time is linked to planning, crossing the water, communications and movement security. They are different components, but in the sequence described they must function within the same movement.
| Element | What it tested | |---|---| | Planning | weather conditions, bridge and vehicle arrival | | Pontoon engineers | assembly of the floating bridge | | Artillery | crossing of the bridge by the first elements | | Support | communications, medical and logistical equipment, air defense | | Security | information from the ADS 15 drone and general staff procedures |
The first practical point is the interdependence between the phases. Crossing requires the weather conditions to be anticipated, the bridge to be assembled and the vehicles to arrive in coordination. If one of these activities is not ready, the passage described by the source cannot be read as a simple road march: it includes technical work and a sequence of arrivals.
The second concerns the measurement of time. The entry into service of artillery group 49, followed by movement in less than 72 hours, provides a concrete reference for operational speed. The 24-hour motto remains the framework of the exercise; the 72-hour figure instead concerns that group and the transition between service and movement. Separating these two references avoids confusing them.
The third is the territorial scale. The route between Bière and Frauenfeld and the passage through the Vaud Lake Geneva arc, the Fribourg Plateau, the Seeland, the southern foothills of the Solothurn Jura, the Emmental and Upper Aargau show a test distributed across several regions. For the reader, the approximately 300 kilometers have a precise function here: describing the movement. The guide on costo della vita in Svizzera belongs to a different tool on the site. The useful reading remains that of the chain: people, vehicles, bridge, support, reconnaissance and command.

### Five steps
To reconstruct the exercise without mixing up times, equipment and tasks, the reader can use a simple sequence.
1. Personnel and equipment: distinguish clearly between the approximately 3'000 military personnel, the 300 wheeled vehicles and the 50 armored vehicles. The source presents these values as different components of the mobilization. 4. Technical stage: verify the role of pontoon battalion 26 in assembling the floating bridge and the crossing of the first elements of artillery group 49. 5. Operational framework: add mobile communication systems, medical and logistical equipment, air defense, the ADS 15 drone and procedures tested by divisional commander Yves Gächter with his staff.

The same sequence makes it possible to follow the geographical route without turning it into a list of stages extraneous to the source: Vaud's Lake Geneva arc, the Fribourg Plateau, Seeland, the southern foot of the Solothurn Jura, Emmental and Upper Aargau. ## In brief - 136'000 signatures collected for parental leave - 18 weeks of paid leave for mothers and fathers - The signatures will be filed next week - The deadline for collecting the 100'000 signatures expires on the first of October
## Key facts - Proposal → 18 weeks of paid leave for mothers and fathers - Funding → loss-of-earnings insurance - Signatures collected → 136'000 - Filing → next week with the Federal Chancellery - Publication → Federal Gazette, April 2025 - Promoters → Pvl, Verdi, Alliance F, Travail Suisse, Donne del Centro - Support → PS, Evangelical Party and other organizations - Implementation → implementing legislation ready within five years, if accepted
### The political step 136'000 signatures have been collected for the popular initiative on congedo parentale. The Green Liberal Party (Pvl), one of the forces promoting it, announced this. The signatures will be filed next week with the Federal Chancellery. According to the party's statement, the number is sufficient for the initiative to succeed with a comfortable margin.
The required quorum was 100'000 signatures and the deadline for collecting them expires on the first of October. The text of the initiative, entitled «Strong society and economy thanks to parental leave», had been published in the Federal Gazette in April 2025.
The proposal to amend the Constitution is promoted, in addition to Pvl, also by Verdi, Alliance F, Travail Suisse and Donne del Centro. The Socialist Party and the Evangelical Party, together with other organizations, also support the initiative.
### The content of the proposal The text calls for adequate, paid parental leave for mothers and fathers after the birth of the child. Funding should come through loss-of-earnings insurance. If the proposal were accepted, implementing legislation would have to be ready within five years.
For the first ten years, the initiative calls for 18 weeks of leave for both fathers and mothers. The periods should, in principle, be taken one after the other. At most one quarter of the period may be taken together, and the leave will not be transferable from one parent to the other. The phase described by the news is therefore that of collecting and filing the signatures, while the rules on leave belong to the constitutional proposal. The practical point, for those who live or work in Switzerland, is to distinguish the result of the signature collection from the family calendar outlined by the initiative. The quorum brings the proposal to the stage of depositing the signatures. The text, however, links the concrete rules to a possible acceptance and subsequent implementing legislation, specified with a five-year term. The 18 weeks are therefore the duration requested by the proposal and should be read together with this sequence.
### The planned sequence
| Phase | Text's indication | |---|---| | Signature collection | 136'000 announced signatures and deposit next week | | After acceptance | Implementing legislation ready in five years | | First ten years | 18 weeks paid leave for mothers and fathers | | Taking the leave | As a matter of principle, one after the other; at most one quarter together | | Transfer | Not provided for from one parent to the other |
This reading avoids considering the period as a single block that can be freely allocated to the family. The proposal assigns 18 weeks to the mother and 18 weeks to the father, but stipulates that the leaves be taken, as a matter of principle, one after the other. The possibility of staying at home together would exist only for a portion no greater than one quarter of the period provided for. The rule on non-transferability also ties the leave to the parent to whom it is assigned: the text does not allow it to be moved from one position to the other.
### The financing indicated
The reference to loss-of-earnings insurance defines the channel through which, according to the initiative, the leave should be financed. However, the source does not describe an individual procedure, a form, a start date or calculation methods. For the reader, the usable elements are therefore those explicitly stated: the leave would be paid, would concern mothers and fathers, and would have a separate duration for each.
The institutional process also remains linked to the proposed constitutional amendment. The report indicates submission to the Federal Chancellery and subsequent implementing legislation, but does not present differences between Cantons. To follow developments and read the rules described, one can consult the guide on congedo parentale.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. Following the initiative requires a simple distinction between what has already been collected and what depends on the subsequent steps. The source makes it possible to build an informational checklist, without attributing to the reader forms or individual requests that are not described in the text.
### Five steps to keep separate
1. Identify the proposal. The text is entitled «Strong society and economy thanks to parental leave» and calls for adequate and paid leave for mothers and fathers after the birth of the child. The first reference to consult is therefore the one dedicated to congedo parentale.
2. Check the indicated threshold. The initiative required 100'000 signatures. Pvl announced the collection of 136'000 signatures and communicated that the collection deadline expires on the first of October.
3. Follow the submission. The signatures will be submitted next week to the Federal Chancellery. This is the step announced after reaching the quorum; it should not be confused with acceptance of the proposal.
4. Consider the subsequent condition. Only once the initiative has been accepted, according to the text, will the implementing legislation have to be ready in five years. The deadline therefore concerns the legislative phase indicated by the proposal.
5. Read the timetable without changing its rules. For the first ten years, 18 weeks are requested for fathers and 18 for mothers. The periods should in principle be taken one after the other; at most one quarter may be taken together, and leave cannot be transferred from one parent to the other. The planned financing comes through loss-of-earnings insurance.
This sequence makes it possible to correctly interpret the next updates: an announcement about the submission concerns the signatures, whereas any acceptance would open the implementing-legislation phase. The news item does not provide a procedure for submitting an individual request, nor does it indicate documents to submit. To learn more about the proposed process and rules, consult the guide on congedo parentale.
