item.title: Swiss universities: AI changes the assessment of theses
item.description: University of Zurich, ZHAW and SUPSI review examination methods, focusing on oral exams and transparency in the use of artificial intelligence.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Zurich and ZHAW are focusing on oral exams, presentations and thesis defenses - The thesis must also be assessed based on the process, not only the result - SUPSI asks for a more detailed description of AI use
## Key facts - What → rethinking the assessment of written work - Where → University of Zurich and ZHAW - Who → Stefano Peduzzi, lecturer at SUPSI - Objective → verifying the skills actually acquired - New → providing more detailed information about interaction with AI - Detectors → ZHAW and DFA/ASP have chosen not to use them
The University of Zurich and ZHAW are placing greater emphasis on oral exams, presentations and thesis defenses. The choice stems from a simple change to describe: creating summaries, organizing notes and writing a thesis now takes less time when students use artificial intelligence. If the final result can be produced with increasing assistance from technology, assessment cannot focus solely on the submitted document.
The objective is to verify more directly whether the skills have actually been acquired. AI is described as important: anyone looking at annunci di lavoro must also consider the process.
### Why oral exams are not a complete answer
Stefano Peduzzi, a lecturer in the Department of Education and Learning / Teacher Education University of SUPSI and head of the Teaching Diploma for Upper Secondary Schools, recognizes the advantages of oral assessments, but limits their scope.
> «The oral exam can test some essential skills, such as those related to presentation and language».
The thesis, however, requires more: searching for original sources, selecting and evaluating them, and distinguishing relevant information from irrelevant information. For this reason, according to Peduzzi, the oral exam does not cover all the skills required to write a thesis. The limitation is also organizational, because oral exams are difficult to manage in courses with hundreds of students.
The focus thus shifts from the product to the process. It becomes necessary to understand what the student has done independently, how they have used AI and whether, during the work, they have developed the necessary skills. The source does not provide a numerical threshold for measuring this relationship: 2% and 80% alone do not explain the share of work done by the student or AI if it is not clarified what they refer to.
### The approach chosen by SUPSI
ZHAW has decided not to use software to recognize AI-generated texts, considering it insufficiently reliable. A similar choice was made at DFA/ASP of SUPSI, where the difficulty of determining precisely the extent to which the technology has been used is emphasized.
The answer is not prohibition. The department focuses on critical and informed use, with continuous discussion between the student and the supervisor. In the case of the thesis, the limited number of students supervised by each lecturer makes more frequent interaction possible than in a regular classroom. ## From finished text to verifiable work
The change described by Swiss universities modifies the meaning of the thesis. Previously, the submitted document could appear to be the main evidence of the work carried out; now the result must be read together with the decisions, sources and explanations that produced it. The text is not always enough to show how much the student reflected, selected and verified.
### Two levels of the same assessment
| Previous requirement | New verification requirement | |---|---| | Writing summaries and organizing notes | Understanding which choices were made by the student | | Submitting a written thesis | Reconstructing the path that led to the result | | Evaluating the final product | Verifying autonomy, use of AI and skills developed | | Using a detector to look for abuse | Discussing the work stages transparently |
The comparison does not lead to a single rule. An oral exam can assess presentation and language, but it does not cover the research of sources, their selection and the assessment of their relevance. A written exam may remain necessary, especially when the number of students makes it impractical to question everyone. The answer indicated by the source is therefore a balance between different forms of verification: presentations, discussions, oral exams and written work.
This balance also changes the relationship between teacher and student. If the supervisor has to understand how a paper was constructed, recognizable steps and dialogue throughout the thesis are needed, not merely an assessment at the time of submission. The practical consequence is greater attention to motivations: why a source was chosen, why information was considered relevant, which part of the text was developed independently and what assistance AI provided.
### Why the detector does not solve the problem
The choice by ZHAW and DFA/ASP not to use detection software is linked to the difficulty of precisely establishing the degree of AI use and to the low reliability attributed to these tools. Monitoring therefore does not shift to an automated percentage.
For the university, the point is not merely to prove that a text was written without assistance. It is to understand whether the person still knows how to find, select, evaluate and apply information. For the student, this means that the use of AI must be explainable, not simply denied or hidden.
The link with the world of work extends this shift beyond the thesis. The source states that knowing how to use AI is becoming important, but the degree does not replace specialized knowledge. A credible educational path must therefore show both things: familiarity with the tool and the ability to reason without delegating everything to technology. Anyone considering the next step can complement this reflection with aziende che assumono.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to document the thesis process
For a student, the new approach translates into a more traceable workflow. The source already describes the direction chosen by the DFA/ASP: compared to last year, the interaction with AI during the drafting process must be indicated in more detail. From this, a concrete procedure can be derived, built upon the steps that the department asks to be made visible.
### Five steps to make visible
1. Clarify before processing. The first step is to discuss with the supervisor in which phases AI can be used and to what extent. The definition must be transparent and shared. It is not enough to know that the tool is available: its use must be linked to the individual activities of the thesis.
2. Record interactions. During the drafting process, it is advisable to note how AI was used, without reducing everything to the final submission. The more detailed indication requested by the DFA/ASP serves precisely to distinguish what the person did from what was entrusted to technology. The recording should help understand what was actually learned and what, instead, was delegated.
3. Separate skills. The search for original sources, selection, evaluation, and the distinction between pertinent and non-pertinent information remain steps that one must know how to explain. The same applies to decisions made during the work. If AI accelerated an activity, the result must still be understood and applicable independently.
4. Prepare for the discussion. A presentation or a meeting with the supervisor requires illustrating the arguments, justifying choices, and critically analyzing the results. It is precisely these steps that allow for the evaluation of the process, not just the form of the submitted text. The oral exam may probe presentation and language, but the discussion must fit into the broader framework of the thesis.
5. Maintain ongoing dialogue. The relationship with the supervisor does not end with the final revision. The source indicates frequent interaction throughout the process, made possible by the limited number of students supervised by each lecturer. This dialogue allows for the correction of AI use as the work progresses and for the development of a critical and conscious application.
The logic also applies to those preparing for the professional world: knowing how to use AI matters, but it does not replace critical reflection. To transform this awareness into a concrete step toward employment, consult the salary calculator.

On Thursday 24 September 2026, the Swiss National Bank (SNB) decided to keep the reference rate at 0%, the level at which it has stood since June 2025. The choice is linked to the fact that inflation in the Confederation remains under control.
The central bank nevertheless left the door open to intervention in the foreign exchange market, if necessary, to ensure appropriate monetary conditions.
> “If necessary, the National Bank is (...) prepared to intervene in the foreign exchange market to ensure appropriate monetary conditions,” it added in a statement.
The Swiss decision differs from that of the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and the European Central Bank (ECB), which recently increased their reference rates. The Swiss issuing institution therefore chose the monetary status quo.
### Prices, oil and stability
Price dynamics have not remained completely still. The source reports a slight acceleration in inflation, due to the surge in oil prices. Despite this movement, the SNB considers its monetary policy appropriate for keeping inflation within the price stability range and supporting economic activity.
The stated objective is to keep inflation between 0% and 2%. However, the central bank warned that the context surrounding trade policy and exchange-rate developments remain factors of uncertainty.
The same day brought a significant revision of the growth forecasts for gross domestic product. For 2026, the SNB now indicates a range between 1,5% and 2,0%, compared with approximately 1% estimated in mid-June during the previous quarterly analysis of the country’s economic and monetary situation. For 2027, the growth of the Swiss economy is expected to stand at more or less 1,5%.
Inflation projections were also revised upwards by around ten basis points: 0,7% for the current year and 0,8% for the following year. The SNB attributes the update to the increase in petroleum product prices, which was stronger than expected. Inflation is expected to stabilize at this level in 2028; the estimates remain conditional on maintaining a reference rate of zero throughout the period under consideration. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical value of the decision lies in the combination of continuity and caution. The SNB did not announce a new rate level: it confirmed the one already in force. At the same time, it signaled that oil, trade policy, and exchange rates may alter the observed framework in upcoming updates.
The source thus provides a basis for reading the cost of living in Switzerland, but not a personalized calculation for every household or business. The comparison with the Fed and ECB adds a second level of reading. item.title: Extension of duty exemption for fodder maize until April 2027
item.description: The DEFR extends until 30 April 2027 the duty exemption for fresh or silage maize with dry matter ≤60%, intended for animal feed; from 1 October 2026 duty reduction for fibre-rich fodder.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Summer drought: less hay and maize in many regions - DEFR: duty exemption for maize until 30 aprile 2027 - Initial measure of 15 agosto 2026, initially until the end of October - From 1 ottobre 2026, reduced duties on other fibrous forage
## Key facts - Publication → 25 settembre 2026 - Authority → DEFR - Measure → duty exemption - Product → maize, fresh or ensiled - Destination → animal feed - Expiry → 30 aprile 2027 - Requirement → dry matter not exceeding 60 percent - Permit → general import permit
The announcement published in Bern on 25 settembre 2026 updates the federal response to the drought that affected the forage crop. DEFR has decided to extend the duty exemption for maize, fresh or ensiled, intended for animal feed.
The measure was adopted on 15 agosto 2026 to facilitate imports and support the farms directly affected. The exemption, initially applicable until the end of ottobre 2026, concerns maize with a dry matter content not exceeding 60 percent. The new expiry date is 30 aprile 2027.
### The DEFR decision
The request for an extension came from the Swiss Farmers' Union, referred to in the announcement by the abbreviation USC. DEFR points to logistical difficulties in cross-border transport: this very factor weighed on the decision to extend the duration of the relief.
The decision is part of an agricultural season marked by very different conditions. A spring favorable to vegetation growth was followed by a summer characterized by drought. In most regions, the phenomenon negatively affected hay production and maize yields. The scant rainfall in August and September improved the situation only to a limited extent.
The announcement distinguishes maize intended for animals from other forage products. With effect from 1 ottobre 2026, customs duties on certain high-fiber forage products, usable as substitutes for roughage, will also be reduced. For these products, DEFR places the measure within the ordinary monthly update of customs duties.
For those reading the provision, the central point is therefore the two-part timing: a duty exemption for maize meeting the stated requirements, extended until 30 aprile 2027, and a reduction in duties for certain high-fiber forage products from 1 ottobre 2026. The two provisions are presented separately and do not have the same wording. ## What changes operationally
The extension modifies the timetable according to which an import of forage can be assessed. For maize, the criterion is not only the animal destination: the text also links the exemption to the form of the product, fresh or ensiled, and to a dry matter content not exceeding 60 percent. The date to keep in mind for the application is April 30, 2027.

## In brief - 25 September 2026: 334.5 million francs allocated - PIC 4: 66.9 million per year from 2028 to 2032 - More funding for language, education and employment - Employment of immigrants at 77% in the OECD area
## Key facts - Decision → total commitment credit of 334.5 million francs - Period → 2028-2032 - PIC 4 → 66.9 million francs per year - Cantons → 37.3 million francs per year for the PICs - National programmes → 29.6 million francs per year - PIC 3 → ends at the end of 2027 - PIC 4 basic document → adopted on 18 September 2026
On 25 September 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council announced an increase in federal and cantonal funding for integration promotion. The decision concerns the 2028-2032 period and translates into a total commitment credit of 334.5 million francs for the cantonal integration programmes, the PICs, and for other programmes and projects of national importance.
For PIC 4, the Confederation is planning 66.9 million francs per year for integration measures. The increase compared with the current period is 5.4 million per year. The statement links the increase in funding to the need to enable a greater number of people to benefit from integration promotion.
The allocation distinguishes between cantonal programmes and initiatives of national scope. The Cantons are allocated 37.3 million francs per year for the PICs, with priority given to language promotion, information and counselling, as well as educational and professional integration. The cantonal contribution to the financing of PIC 4 must be at least equal to that of the Confederation.
### Objectives set with the Cantons
The PIC 4 basic document indicates two main directions: removing barriers to the integration of women and making greater use of educational pathways for lasting integration into the labour market. The document was drawn up jointly by the Confederation and the Cantons and adopted on 18 September 2026 by the plenary assembly of the Conference of Cantonal Governments, the CdC.
The Confederation is also planning 29.6 million francs per year for national programmes and projects. Among these, the statement mentions the Integration pre-apprenticeship, PTI, designed to make better use of the potential of the domestic workforce.
Since 2014, the PICs have been the central instrument of Swiss integration policy: they coordinate promotion efforts in the Cantons and facilitate immigrants' access to language, education, the labour market and social participation. The figure given for immigrant employment is 77 per cent, one of the highest rates in the OECD area. PIC 3 ends at the end of 2027. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the decision has an impact that is apparent above all in the continuity of the system. PIC 3 end at the end of 2027; the new cycle covers 2028 to 2032. The transition is not presented as an isolated measure, but as a strengthening of the programs that, since 2014, have coordinated the promotion of integration in all cantons.
The first practical level is linguistic and informational. The resources allocated to the PICs concern language promotion, information and counseling. These are the areas indicated in the press release to support access to training, the labor market and social participation. To find one's bearings on the employment side, one can consult annunci di lavoro, while the federal decision identifies educational and professional pathways as a priority. The text does not describe an individual hiring procedure.
There is also a national channel distinct from the cantonal one. The 29,6 million francs per year for programs and projects of national importance include the PTI and aim to harness the potential of the domestic workforce. item.title: Zug: economic promotion halted, 272 apartments under 1800 francs
item.description: Urban Keiser (Korporation Zug) calls for an end to economic promotion: unsustainable growth, skyrocketing rents. 272 homes at <1800 CHF, long waiting list. Elections 4 October.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Urban Keiser calls for an end to economic promotion in Zug - Korporation Zug is building 272 affordable apartments - A 3,5-room apartment costs less than 1800 francs - Canton elections will be held on 4 October
## Key facts - Who → Urban Keiser, president of Korporation Zug - Where → Canton Zug - What → End to economic promotion - Housing → 272 apartments - Rent → Less than 1800 francs for 3,5 rooms - Elections → 4 October - Outlook → Population increasing by 50% in 20 years
The 61-year-old Urban Keiser, president of Korporation Zug, is calling for an end to economic promotion in the canton of Zug. In his view, growth has driven housing costs up to an intolerable level. The statement is contained in an interview published by Tages-Anzeiger.
Korporation Zug is a public-law community similar to a Ticinese patriziato, but extending across the entire canton. It is the canton’s largest landowner and builds affordable apartments.
### An offer that is not enough
Keiser recalls that until about 20 years ago, local residents were able to find housing. Today, it has become difficult. For this reason, the corporation is developing a residential complex with 272 apartments. The rent for a 3,5-room apartment costs less than 1800 francs and immediately generated a long waiting list.
The allocation follows clear criteria. Keiser cites minimum occupancy and explains that people who grew up in Zug have priority. He admits that this choice might not be politically correct, but says that the corporation proceeds this way.
The city’s catchment area, according to the interviewee, is the entire world. He points to three reasons: low taxes, a safe environment and enchanting landscapes. In his view, 100'000 apartments could be built and all of them sold. Since demand cannot be met, it remains possible to manage the allocation.
Keiser says he has almost no contact with the Expats, high-income foreign workers who converge on Zug. He acknowledges the decline of German in some places, the changing nature of urban life and the loss of customs, such as selling the Carnival newspaper early in the morning. «These things cannot be stopped», he maintains.
### Incentives and crafts
Regarding growth, Keiser replies: «Absolutely not. In fact, economic incentives could be abolished altogether». He criticizes the welcome given to new companies: when a start-up or cryptocurrency company arrives in Zug, the state council almost as a whole goes to shake hands. In his carpentry business, which is nearly 100 years old, he would not have seen anyone. Craftspeople would by now be a curiosity. ## The growth fueling the housing crisis
The story of Zug sets two effects of the same policy against each other: economic attractiveness and the difficulty of finding a home. Growth creates demand, but housing availability does not keep pace. For those observing the cost of living in Switzerland, the concrete issue is the relationship between an affordable rent and demand far exceeding supply.
The interview describes a city capable of attracting people from all over the world thanks to low taxes, a safe environment and enchanting landscapes. The pressure therefore concerns not only those looking for a new home. It also concerns the possibility of allocating housing when the number of requests exceeds the number of available homes.
### Land, regulations and timeframes
Keiser argues that only those who own land can build housing and observes that politicians, obviously, do not. The criticism concerns the transition from promises to implementation: according to him, the corporation sees no concrete evidence of the support it received, while regulations are being tightened.
In the case described, the result would be slower and more expensive construction. The corporation reportedly experienced this with a project dragged out for 20 years. For a family or a worker looking for a home, such long timeframes make future availability uncertain and leave the waiting list as a sign of the existing pressure.

## In brief
- No federal minimum wage; some Cantons have one - Maximum working hours: 45 or 50 hours per week - Permits: L, B, C and G with different durations
## Key facts
- Minimum wage → no federal level; some Cantons have one - Maximum working hours → 45 hours in industry, offices and retail; 50 in other sectors - Holidays → 4 weeks; 5 for those under 20 - Maternity/paternity → 14 weeks at 80%; 2 weeks - SEM permits → L, B, C and G - Notice period → 1, 2 or 3 months depending on length of service - LAMal → mandatory for residents within 3 months of arrival - Rent → maximum deposit of 3 months' rent
### The framework to check before applying
Switzerland has no federal minimum wage: some Cantons have their own. For anyone looking for a job in 2026, the first thing to put in order is therefore the scope of the offer: the national market, cantonal rules and personal circumstances do not automatically coincide.
The search can start on job portals and with a Swiss CV tailored to the job posting, but the decisive step is to read the contract together with the rules that affect salary and residence. The focus on the canton of Lucerne should be read within the national framework: tax conditions and some aspects of daily life depend on the Canton and the municipality, while many labor rules are federal. The annunci di lavoro are used to compare duties and conditions before the interview, without confusing the job title with the available net pay.
Maximum working hours are 45 per week for industry, offices and retail, and 50 hours in other sectors. The minimum holiday entitlement is four weeks, rising to five for those under 20. Maternity leave lasts 14 weeks at 80% through IPG; paternity leave lasts two weeks. In the event of notice, the periods are one month in the first year, two months from the second to the ninth, and three months from the tenth year.
For social insurance, AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG come into the reading of the payslip: the AVS/AI/IPG share payable by the employee is 5.3%, while the total including the employer is 10.6%. AD/AC is 1.1% up to the annual maximum; LAINF/LAA ranges from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. LPP/BVG applies, to the coordinated salary, rates of 7% between ages 25 and 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from age 55 until reference age.
For a foreign national, SEM distinguishes the short-term L permit, up to one year, the renewable B residence permit, the C settlement permit and the G permit for cross-border commuters. The C is normally linked to ten years of residence, reduced to five for EU/EFTA citizens. It is these steps, more than the interview alone, that turn an application into a sustainable work project. ### Net pay does not equal gross pay
A proposal for Lucerne should be compared with an offer in another Canton starting from the three tax components: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each Canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax. A nationwide comparison cannot be completed by looking at a single tax rate.
| Area | Rule | What to check | |---|---|---| | Taxation | Federal, cantonal and municipal IFD | Canton and municipality of the offer | | Healthcare | Mandatory LAMal/KVG for residents | premium by canton or region, deductible and subsidy | | Housing | federal law the same in every Canton | deposit, blocked account and form |
The roles of the institutions must be kept separate. AFC/ESTV is the reference for direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations are responsible for cantonal and municipal taxation. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS, AI and LPP, but does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not decide tax rates. This map reduces the risk of using a statistical figure as a tariff or a social contribution as a tax.
The cost of living also requires separate consideration. LAMal/KVG is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums are per capita, vary according to canton and region, and are neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. Regarding housing, the rule is federal and the same in every Canton: the security deposit cannot exceed three months' rent and must be held in a blocked account in the tenant's name. The landlord's notice is valid only on the official cantonal form; the challenge must be submitted within 30 days to the conciliation authority. ## Key facts - Date: 25 September 2026 - Location: Bern - Authority: SECO - Diesel: all-time high - Petrol: more than two francs per litre - Support mentioned: unemployment insurance and short-time work - Further measures: only in the event of an imminent severe recession
On 25 September 2026, Bern confirmed that, for now, no government intervention to ease the cost of fuel is planned. In recent days, diesel has reached an all-time high; petrol, meanwhile, has been costing more than two francs per litre for some time. At Swiss petrol stations, discontent is being expressed through very harsh comments, while the expense weighs particularly heavily on tradespeople, farmers and commuters.
Calls for public support have become more insistent. Several parliamentarians have turned to the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, led by President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin. The position indicated for the department is clear: intervention to ease the situation is ruled out.
### The Confederation's position
Thomas Knutti, an SVP national councillor and co-owner of a transport company, has repeatedly criticised the Federal Council's caution. He recalled having requested relief measures in March and submitted a parliamentary question in June, without being heeded.
Asked by 20 Minuten, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs explained that high prices are not merely a cost. In SECO's view, they must signal the scarcity of fuel and guide behaviour.
> «In the current context, it is essential that fuel prices signal scarcity: this encourages saving, turning to alternatives, increasing efficiency and investing in different solutions».
According to the authority, government intervention would remove the incentive to take precautions independently and weaken the economy's resilience. SECO also wants to avoid generalised measures. No precise threshold for diesel or petrol is given: the criterion would be the performance of the economy as a whole. To track the impact of rising prices on everyday expenses, one can consult the costo della vita in Svizzera. For motorists, therefore, the issue is not only the price recorded at the pump, but also the absence of a public response linked to that price. The announced outlook remains that of an expensive fill-up, at least until the economic picture changes. ## The price does not trigger a threshold
For those who live or work in Switzerland and depend on a car, the message has an immediate effect: filling up remains an expense exposed to the market, and no relief tied to a precise figure is planned. This directly concerns the categories indicated by the source, namely tradespeople, farmers and commuters. For them, the increase in fuel becomes part of travel or business costs; for motorists, the announced consequence is that filling up will remain expensive.
The second consequence concerns expectations. SECO does not indicate a diesel or gasoline price limit above which federal intervention would automatically be triggered. The reference point is the economy as a whole. A record price at the pump, on its own, is not presented as a sufficient condition for changing policy.
### Three scenarios indicated by the source
| Situation | Indicated response | | High prices in the current framework | Incentives for savings, alternatives, efficiency and investment in different solutions | | Economic slowdown | First, unemployment insurance and compensation for reduced working hours | | Serious imminent recession | Assessment of further economic policy measures |
The sequence shows why the political debate is not reduced to the cost per liter. On the one hand, there is the immediate impact on the budgets of those who have to travel or work with fuel. On the other hand, there is SECO's view that a high price preserves a scarcity signal and encourages people to prepare independently. Generalized aid would weaken that signal and, in the authority's assessment, undermine the economy's resilience.
The source does not describe a specific measure for one category; instead, it presents a federal choice linked to the general economic situation. No emergency threshold has been communicated for the price of gasoline or diesel. For those who need to plan travel or work-related costs, practical guidance can therefore be based on the criteria SECO has made public, without turning them into a promise of aid.
### Four steps
1. Assess exposure. Artisans, farmers and commuters are the categories identified as most affected by fuel costs. If one falls into one of these categories, the price increase is reflected in travel or operating costs.
2. Do not wait for an automatic threshold. SECO has not indicated a diesel or gasoline price that would trigger an intervention. The record high reached by diesel, on its own, therefore does not create an announced measure.
3. Look at the economy as a whole. According to the authority, this is the criterion for assessing the situation. The price at the pump signals fuel scarcity, but the public decision would depend on the overall trend.
4. Distinguish between the two levels of response. In the event of a slowdown, the source first cites unemployment insurance and compensation for reduced working hours. Only in the face of an imminent severe recession would additional economic policy measures be considered. At present, SECO says there are no signs pointing in this direction.
This sequence does not reduce the price of a tankful and does not replace a public decision. It serves to read the news correctly: no relief has been announced, no published threshold exists, and the stated criterion is the resilience of the economy. ## In brief
- 2026 GDP: +1.7%, compared to +0.9% in June - 2027 GDP: +1.7%, up from the previous +1.5% - 2026 Inflation: 0.6%, down from the previous 0.7% - 2026 Unemployment: 3.1%
## Key facts

The KOF of the Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH Zurich) has detected a clear improvement in Swiss business outlook for the current year. The new survey, conducted among the country’s economists, raises the 2026 gross domestic product growth forecast, net of sports-related effects, to +1.7%. In June, the expectation was +0.9%. 2027 is also viewed more favorably: the estimate rises to +1.7%, from the previously indicated +1.5%.
### Prices and labor market
The revision does not only concern growth. Inflation estimates have been revised downward: in 2026, prices are expected to rise by 0.6%, compared to 0.7% in the June survey. For 2027, the forecast is 0.7%, down from the previous 0.8%; in five years, it stands at 0.8%, down from 0.9%. On the labor market, however, prospects remain virtually unchanged. The unemployment rate is seen at 3.1% in 2026, at 3% in the following twelve months, and at 2.9% in five years.
The survey thus compares different time horizons: the current year for GDP and inflation, 2027 for growth and prices, twelve months for certain exchange rates and the stock index, and five years for price and unemployment outlooks.
The euro-swiss franc exchange rate, which has risen in the last two months, is expected to remain substantially stable. The rate is forecast at 0.93 in three months and 0.92 in one year; for the dollar, the indicated average values are 0.81 and 0.80. Those following conversions can compare these two deadlines in the CHF/EUR comparator.
On the stock market, specialists are more cautious than in June. The SPI index is expected at approximately 19,725 points in one quarter, slightly below the current level, and at 20,633 points in twelve months. The estimates are part of the 123rd KOF Consensus Forecast, in which 17 experts participated, interviewed between September 3 and 23. The survey should not be confused with the forecasts of the business cycle center itself nor with its barometer. ## Practical reading for those who live and work in Switzerland
The comparison with June is the starting point for interpreting the revision. The growth forecast for 2026 rises from +0,9% to +1,7%, while that for 2027 increases from +1,5% to +1,7%. The change describes an improvement in experts’ expectations, not an already recorded result. For this reason, the figure should be read as a reference scenario for the Swiss economy.
### Prices, employment and different time horizons
The section on inflation requires a simple distinction. When the estimate falls from 0,7% to 0,6% for 2026, this does not mean that prices are expected to decrease: the source still indicates an increase. Instead, the revision signals a more contained expected increase compared with June. The same interpretation applies to the change from 0,8% to 0,7% in 2027 and from 0,9% to 0,8% in five years. The survey does not break down the figure by individual expenses, so it does not make it possible to derive the trend of a specific item in a personal budget. The labor market offers a distinct trajectory. The 3,1% forecast for 2026 falls to 3% in the following twelve months and to 2,9% in five years, but the source defines the prospects as virtually unchanged. The figure, therefore, does not describe the outcome for a single profession or a specific area of the country. It only shows the overall direction indicated by experts.

Forecasts can become a personal monitoring sheet if indicators and deadlines are kept separate. The method remains faithful to the source: record the values, compare them with June, and do not transform a collective estimate into an individual data point.
### Five-step procedure
1. Set the GDP horizon. Mark 2026 with +1.7% and 2027 with +1.7%; next to it, keep the June references of +0.9% and +1.5% so the comparison remains readable.
2. Create a separate row for prices. For 2026, note 0.6%; for 2027, 0.7%; and for five years, 0.8%. Place the previous values of 0.7%, 0.8%, and 0.9% nearby, without confusing them.

5. Keep the stock market separate. Write 19,725 points for the SPI in one quarter and 20,633 in twelve months, remembering that the first estimate is slightly below the current level.
### Periodic verification
When updating the sheet, always check three elements: the time horizon, the comparison with June, and the nature of the figure, ensuring it is a survey forecast. item.title: Cembra and Vontobel leave Zurich: taxes and space drive the move
item.description: Cembra moves 660 employees to Baden (15% taxes) in autumn 2027; Vontobel brings 1.500 jobs to Baar (12%) by 2030. Zurich at 20%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Cembra will transfer 660 employees to Baden in the autumn of next year. - Vontobel will move its headquarters and 1’500 employees to Baar by 2030. - Corporate taxation in Baden is 15%. - In Zurich it is almost 20%; in Baar it falls to 12%.
- Cembra → 660 employees in Baden, canton Aargau - Cembra relocation → autumn of next year - Vontobel → headquarters and 1’500 employees to Baar by 2030 - Taxation in Baden and Zurich → 15% and almost 20% - Taxation in Baar → 12%
### Two announcements close together
The 12.30 news bulletin of 25 settembre 2026 opens with two relocations that are sparking debate in Zurich’s financial center. Following the announcement by Vontobel, a private bank that will move its headquarters to the canton of Zug, news arrived on Thursday of Cembra: the company will instead move its headquarters to Aargau. These are two departures within a few weeks, and in Zurich many see them as a warning sign.
Cembra will move to Baden with its 660 employees in the autumn of next year. The distance from its current headquarters remains short: Baden is fifteen minutes away by train. The official justification does not mention taxes. The company cites infrastructure and modern offices, as well as the possibility of growing in a location that remains central. The report notes that there is no mention of tax savings.
The savings, however, emerge from the comparison reported in the news bulletin. Corporate taxation in Baden is 15%, whereas in Zurich it is almost 20%. Based on the 2025 financial statements, for Cembra the difference amounts to 10 million francs less to pay. This is the figure that makes the tax issue concrete, even though the company publicly presents other reasons for its choice.
The calculation is even more apparent for Vontobel. By 2030 the bank will move its headquarters and 1’500 employees to Baar, in the canton of Zug, where taxation falls to 12%. On the news bulletin, Christian Bretscher, director of the Association of Zurich Bankers, downplays the idea of a problem for the financial center:
> «Not from the point of view of the financial center,» Christian Bretscher, director of the Association of Zurich Bankers, tells RSI’s news bulletin.
In his view, the two banks want to invest in Zurich’s financial center, which for some time has no longer coincided solely with the boundaries of the city or canton.
The political reading is different. The SVP and FDP are calling for a political response and more favorable conditions for businesses. Bretscher agrees that there are two pressures: higher taxation than in neighboring cantons and the availability of space and offices. According to the Association of Bankers, these are the signals to which Zurich must pay attention. ## The tax comparison does not automatically concern the individual resident
### Separating corporate taxes and personal circumstances
The first clarification concerns the party involved. The article discusses company locations, employees and taxation for businesses; it does not announce a new rule for taxpayers. For those who live or work in Switzerland, therefore, the move should not be presented as a change to AVS/AHV, LPP/BVG, LAMal/KVG, the minimum wage or the cost of living: the source does not describe changes in any of these areas.
The Swiss tax framework also requires distinguishing three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each Canton has its own law and its own multiplier; municipalities apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax. The percentages mentioned for Baden, Zurich and Baar are therefore a territorial comparison of corporate taxation, not figures to be automatically applied to an individual's tax return. The article does not break down those figures across the three levels or provide a municipal multiplier.
To get one’s bearings regarding the personal aspect, calcolatore stipendio e imposte may be useful for examining one’s income, but it does not authorize using corporate tax rates as though they were individual rates.
The second practical point concerns competition among Cantons. The source places tax pressure and the availability of space and offices side by side: a more affordable location is not described merely as an accounting choice. The distinction between the official rationale and the calculated savings must be maintained when assessing the news. In Cembra’s case, the article in fact pairs infrastructure, modern offices, room for growth and a central location with the comparison of taxes.
On the political level, UDC and PLR are calling for more favorable conditions for businesses, while the bankers’ association points to taxation and space as concrete problems. No political decision is announced. The two departures are therefore a signal to monitor for Zurich’s business center, not a new rule for families and workers.

### Four checks before drawing conclusions
Anyone who needs to use this data to guide a decision can follow a simple sequence. The first rule is to establish whether one is analyzing a company, the location of its headquarters, or an individual's personal tax situation: the service does not place these aspects on the same level.
1. Separate the subject. For a company, note the canton and the location of its headquarters; for an employee, keep their own situation separate from that of their employer. The tax rates reported by the service are presented for companies and should not automatically be used for individual income.
2. Divide the comparison into two columns. The first should contain the tax conditions indicated by the service; the second, the operational elements: infrastructure, modern offices, growth opportunities, and central location. This avoids reducing every relocation to a single percentage, when the official rationale also includes space and organizational factors.
3. Identify the correct contact. In the general framework, AFC/ESTV manages direct federal tax and VAT, while the cantonal administrations handle the cantonal and municipal parts. Each Canton has its own law and multiplier. However, the source does not indicate a form, procedure, or administrative deadline for headquarters relocations: steps that the service does not provide must not be added.
4. Check the dates without anticipating the effects. Cembra indicates the autumn of next year; Vontobel sets the relocation for no later than 2030. The text quantifies the employees involved, but does not mention layoffs, salaries, contracts, or changes in benefits. For those working at the two banks, the prudent approach is to follow company communications and not turn the relocation of the headquarters into an already-decided employment outcome.

item.title: Ticino's healthcare system needs new incentives
item.description: Covid has left extraordinary and lasting costs; health insurers retain at most 5% of expenditure; up to one fifth of healthcare spending is linked to unnecessary services.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ticino: the healthcare trajectory is worrying. - Covid generated extraordinary and long-lasting costs. - Health insurers may retain a maximum of 5%. - Up to one fifth of spending may be linked to unnecessary services.
## Key facts - Author → Matteo Galgiani, vice-president PLR Terre di Pedemonte - Area → Swiss healthcare, with particular focus on Ticino - Pressure indicated → extraordinary and long-lasting costs linked to Covid - Administrative spending → maximum 5% of healthcare spending - Numerical example → from 10 to 20 billion: 5% from 500 million to 1 billion - Estimate cited → up to one fifth of spending on unnecessary services - Drugs mentioned → GLP-1-based products against obesity
Matteo Galgiani, vice-president PLR Terre di Pedemonte, describes Swiss healthcare and, with particular emphasis, healthcare in Ticino as a system on a worrying trajectory. The crisis caused by Covid generated extraordinary and long-lasting costs. According to the author, however, the problem is broader: under the current model, none of the actors has a genuine interest in solving it. Every incentive designed for one party triggers blame-shifting onto the others and blocks reforms.
### The patient and spending
High insurance premiums and a mechanism that, once the deductible and cost-sharing have been exceeded, allows practically unlimited and free access to services often encourage patients to seek treatment. The very broad catalogue offers services with real or perceived benefits. For the insurance side, guida alla cassa malati can be consulted. Citizens remain the weak link: they vote and decide, but they do not have the bargaining power or resources of large lobbies, including pharmaceutical companies and health insurers.
Health insurers may retain a maximum of 5% of healthcare spending for administration. If spending increases, the absolute share also increases: in the source’s example, from 10 to 20 billion francs, 5% rises from 500 million to 1 billion. For an individual insurer, stopping an unnecessary service may cost more than the savings; for the system, rising spending benefits all insurers.
### Supply, profit and arbitrage
Doctors, pharmacists, hospitals and physiotherapists must ensure themselves a stable income. The system offers no concrete incentive to reject unnecessary or superfluous treatments: accommodating demand prevents patients from being lost to more lenient colleagues. Hospitals, also guided by financial objectives, may prioritize quantity over usefulness. The source links a healthcare «bubble» to this mechanism and indicates that up to one fifth of spending is tied to unnecessary services, with risks, contraindications or side effects.
Pharmaceutical companies are presented according to a profit-maximization logic: innovative and profitable drugs, often expensive, do not necessarily coincide with a healthier population. For GLP-1 products against obesity, the source reports that in the vast majority of cases, within one year of discontinuation, much of the lost weight is regained. Galgiani therefore calls for incentives oriented towards public health, non-excessive rewards and mediation by federal and cantonal politics, to avoid family stress and an increase in demand for mental healthcare. ## Where responsibility breaks down
Galgiani’s thesis translates into a practical question: who profits when a service is provided, and who bears the cost when that service is unnecessary? The source does not point to a single command center. Instead, it describes a chain in which patients, health insurers, providers, hospitals and pharmaceutical companies respond to different incentives. For those living in Switzerland, the most visible effect comes through premiums and the burden they place on the cost of living.
### A map of the incentives
| Actor | Incentive described | Effect indicated | |---|---|---| | Patients | Practically unlimited access after the deductible and cost-sharing | Demand for care even for benefits that are only perceived | | Health insurers | Administrative share linked to overall spending | Savings may be lower than the cost of blocking unnecessary services | | Providers | Need for a stable income | Tendency to accommodate demand | | Hospitals | Financial objectives | Priority given to the quantity of services | | Pharmaceutical companies | Profit maximization | Innovative, profitable products for prolonged use |
The table makes the short circuit visible: each behavior may be understandable for the individual actor, but the collective outcome is growing expenditure. The patient seeks a benefit; the professional protects their income; the hospital looks to quantity; the insurer assesses the cost of oversight; the industry pursues profitability. Responsibility is distributed, and no one alone has the leverage to correct the entire process.
The numerical comparison concerning health insurers clarifies the difference between an unchanged percentage and a higher absolute outlay. The 5% remains the same, but on 20 billion it produces 1 billion instead of 500 million on 10 billion. For a family, rising premiums can become a source of psychological stress; the source links this stress to greater demand for mental health care, fueling a negative spiral. The issue therefore concerns not only insurers’ accounts, but also the relationship between healthcare spending and the cost of living.
For the Cantons and federal policy, the practical consequence indicated by the intervention is the need to mediate between lobbies, professional associations and the electorate. A reform oriented toward a single group risks producing more buck-passing. A shared solution should instead assess whether the incentive keeps the population healthy and whether it prevents excessive premiums. Those who want to explore the family dimension can use the costo della vita in Svizzera as a starting point.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From principle to action
The source does not propose a single technical measure, but indicates a criterion: every decision should steer actors toward a healthy population and toward premiums that are not excessive. To turn this criterion into a personal check, one can use a checklist built around the mechanisms described by Galgiani.
### Four steps for evaluating a service
1. Define the benefit. Faced with a treatment or service in the healthcare catalog, ask what concrete benefit is expected. The distinction between real and perceived benefit is the first filter indicated by the source: broad access alone does not demonstrate that a service is necessary.
2. Clarify usefulness and risks. Before signing up, ask the provider to explain why the service is useful, what contraindications it has and what side effects it entails. The source reminds us that unnecessary treatments can carry risks, even when they are requested or offered.
3. Look to the horizon. If the decision concerns GLP-1-based drugs for obesity, distinguish the immediate effect from continuity of use. The intervention points to the regain of much of the lost weight within a year of discontinuation, in the vast majority of cases, and describes continuous and prolonged use.
4. Separate the costs. In the personal budget, distinguish insurance premiums, deductible and cost-sharing. These are the elements that the source relates to the propensity to seek care. To explore the insurance topic further, the guida alla cassa malati is available.
### A criterion for reading proposals
When evaluating a policy solution, the operational question is whether it changes the incentives of all actors or merely shifts the cost from one side to the other. The criterion indicated by Galgiani brings together public health and the sustainability of premiums, without losing sight of lobbies, trade associations and the electorate. A proposal is consistent with this approach when it reduces reliance on unnecessary services, limits buck-passing and does not fuel family stress and demand for mental healthcare.

item.title: VAT at 0,2% and a 24-billion defense fund: the compromise for the States
item.description: With 25 votes against 17, the Council of States approves +0.2 percentage points VAT for 18 years, a defense fund of up to 24 billion and borrowing of up to 12 billion. Reduction of F-35s to ~30 and additional credit of 394 million.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Council of States approves the compromise by 25 votes to 17 - VAT would rise by 0.2 percentage points for 18 years - The defense fund would reach 24 billion - The population will also have to vote on VAT
## Key facts - Decision → Council of States - Vote → 25 to 17 - VAT → +0.2 points for 18 years - Fund → up to 24 billion - Fund debt → up to 12 billion - F-35 → from 36 to around 30 - Additional credit → 394 million francs - Next steps → National Council and popular vote
With 25 votes to 17, the Council of States approved a proposal providing for a temporary increase in VAT and a fund to finance military purchases. It is a step forward, not the end of the matter.
Now it is the National Council’s turn. On the VAT increase, the final say will rest with the population: the compromise is still going through parliamentary and popular procedures.
### The Council of States’ compromise
The Government had proposed a 0.5-percentage-point increase in VAT for 12 years. The Council of States chose 0.2 points for the next 18 years. The compromise also provides for a Fund for Security and Defense, with a maximum capacity of 24 billion and the possibility of incurring debt of up to 12 billion, compared with the 6 billion proposed by the Government. The financing would come from VAT, half of the ordinary financing surpluses and other contributions from the federal budget.
On Modem, the exchange between national councillors Martin Candinas, of the Centre, and Bruno Storni, of the PS, showed the political divide. Candinas considers it necessary to have the resources for investments, while acknowledging the problems that emerged in managing some purchases. Storni, on the other hand, questions the army’s ability to use the resources already available effectively. “Before giving new money, one should see that the money they already have is being managed well,” he stated. He also recalled that the army’s budget has increased since 2022 and that, including military expenditures outside the budget, such as those linked to the militia army, it would come to around 1% of GDP.
The divide also runs through the right-wing parties: in the Council of States, the UDC appeared more willing than the PLR to accept new taxes for the army, while the Radical Liberals prioritized savings. Candinas argued that the PLR and UDC should be ready to raise taxes in order to have a strong army.
The procurement issue is weighing on confidence. The source cites delays and additional costs for F-35s, Israeli drones and the modernization of Duro vehicles. In 2020, the maximum credit of 6 billion for the new fighter aircraft was approved with 50.1% of the vote; the Federal Council then chose 36 F-35s. After the 2022 contract, it emerged in 2025 that the price considered fixed by Bern was not guaranteed by the United States. At the end of June, the Confederation estimated additional costs of between 650 million and 1.3 billion, while the Federal Council reduced the purchase to around 30 fighter jets and requested an additional credit of 394 million. With Martin Pfister at the head of the DDPS in 2025, a new phase began, also marked by the departure of key figures.
To compare a personal simulation without treating the proposal as already in force, calcolatore stipendio e imposte is available. ## The practical reading of the compromise
For those living in Switzerland, the question is not yet which rate to apply: passage through the National Council and a popular vote are still pending. The practical reading consists of separating duration, source of funding and size of the fund. The two proposals have different timelines and profiles.
### Two variants compared
| Item | Government | Council of States | |---|---|---| | VAT increase | 0.5 percentage points for 12 years | 0.2 percentage points for 18 years | | Fund | proposed borrowing of up to 6 billion | borrowing of up to 12 billion | | Open step | National Council and popular vote | National Council and popular vote |
The comparison does not make it possible to calculate how the cost of living for a family would change: reference rates, amounts per individual purchase and an annual estimate per taxpayer are missing. It does, however, make it possible to identify the point to monitor: the compromise concerns the size of the VAT increase, the timing and recourse to borrowing.
The management of procurement is also a variable in the debate. The delays and additional costs cited for F-35, Israeli drones and Duro vehicles have fueled doubts about the ability to use the resources. The issue is therefore twofold: finding additional money and assessing the management of the programs. The text does not present a definitive solution to the second problem.
### GDP, alliances and territory
In the comparison of percentages, the reference figure is 1% of GDP: including military spending outside the budget, Storni already places spending around that threshold. The Swiss objective indicated is to reach 1% of GDP for defense by 2032, almost 9 billion francs a year, compared with the 6.5 billion spent last year.
The international debate also includes 2% of GDP, the threshold recommended by NATO to its members. The source on army financing also indicates that NATO countries are aiming for 5% by 2035. These are international references, not new Swiss rates.
The 80% figure moves the discussion to an operational level. At Meiringen, 80% of fighter-jet takeoffs take place using the afterburner, a procedure much noisier than a standard takeoff. This is information about the use of fighter jets, not an estimate of the fund’s costs.
To follow the possible effect on one’s personal budget without attributing to the proposal a figure that the text does not provide, one can consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the dossier without confusing proposal and decision
The simplest way to read the next updates is to use a checklist with four checks. It serves to avoid conflating the VAT decision, the fund, and the armament programs, which are connected in the dossier but remain separate issues.
### Four checks
1. Status of the procedure. Record separately the vote in the Council of States, the passage to the National Council, and the popular vote on VAT. Do not record 0,2 as an already applicable change: the population still has to express its view.
2. Duration and amount. Put the two parameters of the Council of States' proposal on the same line: 0,2 VAT points and 18 years. On a separate line, retain the Government's proposal: 0,5 points and 12 years. This way, the comparison does not lose the relationship between rate and period.
3. Fund and financing. Check whether the text retains the limit of 24 billion, the power to borrow up to 12 billion, and the specified sources: VAT, half of ordinary financing surpluses, and other contributions from the federal budget. The reference to 6 billion belongs to the Government's proposal.
4. Purchases. Keep the financial verification of the fund separate from the verification of the programs. The text refers to F-35, Israeli drones, and Duro vehicles in connection with delays and additional costs; regarding the F-35, it indicates the reduction from 36 to approximately 30 fighter jets and the need for an additional credit of 394 million.
### What to note in the next steps
The available text does not indicate a date for the debate in the National Council or for the popular vote. The correct check therefore consists of checking when the dossier moves to a different chamber and whether the content remains that approved by the Council of States. There is no need to anticipate an outcome for Parliament or the population: the text points to resistance on both the left and the right.
Until the procedure is concluded, the comparison with the daily budget must remain a simulation. Once there is a final decision, the operational reference may also be the dichiarazione delle imposte. For a personal simulation, use the calcolatore stipendio e imposte.
